title: Grade 3 Social-Emotional Learning & Civics
description: Empathy, emotional regulation, inclusion, active listening, and civic responsibility.

items.prompt: During recess, you notice a new student standing alone watching others play tag. How can you show active inclusion?

options.text: Walk over and invite them to play
Point and whisper about the new student
Ignore them and keep playing tag
Tell them the playground is already full

items.explanation: Inviting a new classmate to play is a kind, inclusive choice.

items.prompt: When you feel overwhelmed or frustrated during a challenging test, what is a healthy self-regulation strategy?

options.text: Rip up the test paper in anger
Take slow breaths and try one item
Yell across the classroom for help
Lay your head down and refuse to try

items.explanation: Slow breaths and focusing on one item help you calm down and keep trying.

items.prompt: What does it mean to be an 'upstander' instead of a 'bystander' when you witness unkind teasing?

options.text: Stand quietly and film with a phone
Join in with the unkind teasing
Speak up kindly and tell a trusted adult
Cheer so the teasing lasts longer

items.explanation: An upstander supports the person being teased and gets adult help.

items.prompt: What is an essential component of active listening when someone is speaking to you?

options.text: Look at your shoes and hold a toy
Talk over the person while they speak
Think about lunch while they speak
Look at them and wait your turn

items.explanation: Active listening means looking at the speaker and not interrupting.

They exist only to give punishments
They exist only to stop all fun
They exist only to fill a poster

items.explanation: Classroom rules keep people safe and help everyone learn fairly.

items.prompt: If you make a promise to clean your pet's cage every Saturday, keeping that promise demonstrates:

options.text: Carelessness
Impulsiveness
Responsibility
Greed

items.explanation: Keeping a promise to care for a pet shows responsibility.

items.prompt: What is an example of showing respect for diverse family structures and backgrounds?

options.text: Judging families that look different
Valuing each family's unique traditions
Telling someone their traditions are wrong
Ignoring cultural heritage months at school

items.explanation: Respect means valuing each family's traditions and caregivers.

items.prompt: How can children participate in civic service in their local neighborhood?

options.text: Leave empty cans in public parks
Write on neighborhood walls and signs
Stay indoors and skip neighborhood days
Help plant trees or donate canned food

items.explanation: Planting trees or donating food helps the neighborhood.

items.prompt: When two friends want to play with the same swing at recess, what is the fairest solution?

options.text: Take turns so both friends get a turn
Push the other person off the swing
Let the taller friend keep the swing
Break the swing so nobody can use it

items.explanation: Taking turns is a fair way to share a swing.

items.prompt: What does having a 'Growth Mindset' mean when learning something difficult?

options.text: Believing you are born smart or not
Quitting as soon as a mistake happens
Believing practice can make you stronger
Never asking a teacher for any help

items.explanation: A growth mindset means effort and practice can help you improve.
